subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should OpenClaw land the linked embedded sessions_spawn guard while this issue remains open for gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn follow-ups, or require a single shared work-spawning policy seam before landing any part?
rationale: The linked PR intentionally changes fallback-turn delegation behavior for one surface and leaves other delegation surfaces uncovered, so automation cannot choose the policy boundary.

options.title: Accept scoped mitigation
options.body: Land or refine the linked embedded sessions_spawn guard and keep this issue open for the remaining surfaces.

options.title: Require one shared seam
options.body: Hold the linked PR until maintainers choose and implement a common fallback completion-announcement policy across work-spawning tools.

options.title: Split ownership first
options.body: Keep the PR paused until maintainers create owner-backed follow-ups for gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped mitigation
recommendation.body: Land or refine the linked embedded sessions_spawn guard and keep this issue open for the remaining surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc already authored the maintainer-facing cross-harness scope review on the linked PR and has recent fallback-area commits.
